name: pia-qbittorrent
description: qBittorrent 5.2.3 combined with Private Internet Access (PIA) VPN, built on Alpine Linux for a minimal footprint. Features: • WireGuard and OpenVPN • Kill switch (IPv4 + IPv6) and DNS leak protection • Auto-healing VPN (reconnects itself if the tunnel drops) • Automatic server failover within your region • PIA port forwarding for better seeding • Correct UID/GID file ownership for Unraid • Configurable UMASK • Multi-arch (amd64 + arm64) Components: • qBittorrent 5.2.3 with libtorrent 2.0.13 • Alpine Linux 3.24, Boost 1.91.0 • OpenVPN 2.7.5, WireGuard 1.0.20260223, iptables 1.8.13 Custom bridge networks work fine (the VPN tunnel runs inside the container either way). Avoid Host networking — the kill switch would firewall the Unraid host itself, not just this container. Extra Parameters must keep --cap-add=NET_ADMIN (required for the VPN + kill switch) and --restart unless-stopped (lets the container auto-restart to recover a dropped VPN connection). Both are set for new installs; if you added this container early, check your Extra Parameters field includes both. Pair with the Windows 11 desktop app: https://github.com/GeorgeAL78/qbittorrent-desktop Fork of j4ym0/pia-qbittorrent with bug fixes and extra features.

variables.name: Port Forwarding
variables.description: Enable PIA port forwarding for better seeding. Falls back gracefully if your region does not support it (e.g. US)

variables.name: UID
variables.description: User ID for qBittorrent process. Use 99 for Unraid nobody

variables.name: GID
variables.description: Group ID for qBittorrent process. Use 100 for Unraid users

variables.name: UMASK
variables.description: Umask for downloads. 000=fully open (recommended for Unraid), 002=group-writable, 022=owner only

variables.name: Web UI Port Variable
variables.description: Must match the port mapping above

variables.name: Web UI Interfaces
variables.description: Comma-separated network interfaces for Web UI access e.g. eth0,eth1 (defaults to the VPN's physical interface)

variables.name: Host Header Validation
variables.description: Set to false if having trouble accessing the WebUI (e.g. behind a reverse proxy)

variables.name: CSRF Protection
variables.description: Set to false if having trouble accessing the WebUI (e.g. behind a reverse proxy)

variables.name: Legacy IPTables
variables.description: Use legacy iptables instead of nftables

variables.name: Extra Subnets
variables.description: Comma-separated extra subnets allowed through the kill switch. Use this if your *arr apps or reverse proxy are on a different Docker network and cannot reach qBittorrent e.g. 172.18.0.0/16

variables.name: Extra LAN Ports
variables.description: Comma-separated extra LAN ports to open e.g. 8989,7878. Use this for containers routed through this one (network_mode: container:...) whose web UI would otherwise be blocked by the kill switch

variables.name: Allow Local Subnet Traffic
variables.description: Set to true to allow LAN devices to connect directly to the container
